item.title: WNBA Finals proves fans tough it out even as leagues don't deserve them
item.description: Atlanta Dream's Angel Reese, right, looks to pass past Golden State Valkyries' Kaitlyn Chen during the first half of Game 6 of the WNBA basketball finals on Thursday, Oct. 29, 2026, in Atlanta. (AP Photo/Brynn Anderson) (Brynn Anderson/Associated Press) The fans found a way. In the middle of a workday, with less than a week's notice, they packed an arena in Atlanta on Thursday, and over breakfast on the other side of the continent they packed a bunch of sports bars, too. No matter how hard those in charge might make it sometimes, lots of folks choose to love the game anyway. Whether the game deserves them or not. This is in part about the WNBA Finals, which soared in popularity despite the baffling ineptitude of the people running them, but it's about much more than that. In the days and weeks leading up to the Atlanta Dream being forced to play a matinee to push the Golden State Valkyries to Saturday night's Game 7, we saw the following developments in other sports: The Milwaukee Brewers, an all-time great team providing a long-suffering fan base with an all-time great moment, prevailed in a feel-good World Series about to give way to what figures to be yet another of Major League Baseball's messy work stoppages . The NBA, continuing to sell both its soul and the financial security of its fan base to the sports gambling industry, added a pair of prediction markets to its list of betting partnerships, all under the guise of "protecting the integrity of the game." The College Football Playoff, looking out for the job security of administrators and coaches more than the interest of either players or viewers, made a move toward expanding toward a 24-team format that almost nobody seems to want . And the NFL kept finding ways to employ players accused of disturbing off-the-field transgressions , even while horrific new alleged details kept emerging about a running back who'd just been cleared to return . It shouldn't be this difficult. It shouldn't be this exhausting. Following your favorite team shouldn't be an exercise in being told, again and again, that your opinion and your scruples and your convenience and your wallet don't matter. Fans watch as players are introduced before Game 6 of the WNBA Finals between the Golden State Valkyries and the Atlanta Dream at State Farm Arena, Thursday, Oct. 29, 2026, in Atlanta, Ga. (Stephen Lam/San Francisco Chronicle via AP) (Stephen Lam/Associated Press) A lack of planning by the people in charge means a potentially title-clinching Game 6 of the WNBA Finals will tip off at 9:30 a.m. on a weekday in the home city of the potential champions? Deal with it. A never-ending string of betting promotions means you can't even watch a game anymore without being repeatedly reminding that your team wants you to lose your paycheck? Deal with it. item.title: Kimmich speaks of difficult comeback after death of his father
item.description: Dortmund's Nico Schlotterbeck embraces Bayern Munich's Joshua Kimmich after the German Bundesliga soccer match between FC Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund at Allianz Arena. (is associated with: «Kimmich speaks of difficult comeback after death of his father») Tom Weller/dpa Bayern Munich midfielder Joshua Kimmich spoke for the first time about the sudden death of his father following the 2-2 Bundesliga draw with Borussia Dortmund on Saturday. "The past week has been very hard for my family, and for me as well. My father was always there for me. He was always by my side. He always supported me and believed in me even when I didn't believe in myself," Kimmich said. "That's why it's really difficult to come back. Because when I'm out on the pitch, that's actually when I think about him the most," said the midfielder, who led Bayern as captain on his return after missing three games. Berthold Kimmich passed away last week at the age of 57. "It was important to come back, to try to get back into a normal daily routine. Even if sometimes you wish the world would just stand still for a bit. But unfortunately - and fortunately - it keeps moving." He added that he was happy to be back with the team and expressed his gratitude for the sympathy and condolences that he and his family have received. "The support from the club, the DFB (German Football Federation), and everyone around us was very special. It meant a great deal to me," he said.

item.title: Aaron Danks provides injury updates on Bayern Munich’s walking wounded
item.description: (Photo by S. Stingl/FC Bayern via Getty Images) | FC Bayern via Getty Images Bayern Munich’s 2-2 draw against Borussia Dortmund came at a potentially significant cost, with three attacking players picking up injuries during Saturday’s encounter. Assistant coach Aaron Danks provided some additional details after the match, althou gh there is still plenty of uncertainty surrounding the extent of the problems. Danks confirmed that Ismael Saibari suffered an ankle injury, while Serge Gnabry appears to have sustained a muscular problem. Michael Olise also experienced discomfort toward the end of the match, but the coaching staff had not yet received a definitive assessment of his condition. “Saibari was the ankle. Gnabry was a muscle injury and I’m unsure with Michael towards the end as well. The physio staff will play a really important role now in helping all the players recover,” Danks said (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ). Danks subsequently offered a slightly more concerning assessment of Saibari’s situation, suggesting that the ankle injury could be particularly serious. “Saibari’s ankle looks quite a serious injury. Serge Gnabry looks muscular, but I’m waiting to find out more. The same with Olise, I haven’t had feedback on that yet,” said Danks. The timing is far from ideal for Bayern, who face Atlétic o Madrid in the Champions League on Tuesday. With Luis Díaz already sidelined and Jamal Musiala still working toward his return, losing additional attacking options would represent another significant headache. For now, Bayern will have to wait for further examinations before determining the availability of al l three players. The medical staff certainly have their work cut ou t. Join the conversation! item.title: Kane laments Dortmund draw after 'incredible high' of Ballon d'Or
item.description: Bayern Munich forward Harry Kane shows off the Ballon d'Or before Saturday's home match with Borussia Dortmund. (Alexandra BEIER) Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane criticised his own performance in Saturday's 2-2 home draw with Borussia Dortmund, just days after the "incredible high" of winning the Ballon d'Or. The draw leaves Bayern and Dortmund deadlocked on 18 points atop the Bundesliga table, with Kane's side ahead on goal difference. Kane won the award in his hometown of London on Monday, the first Englishman since Michael Owen in 2001 and the first Bayern player in 45 years. The 33-year-old said winning the award was "one of the best feelings I've had in my career without a doubt", but said he was frustrated by his own performance on Saturday. The England captain, who took to the pitch wearing boots with gold studs, missed a second-half penalty and it was his wayward pass which Dortmund captain Nico Schlotterbeck intercepted on the way to Dortmund's equaliser. "Today probably wasn't my best performance or the team's best performance, but that's just life," Kane told reporters. "That's just part of being a striker, a footballer. "I probably could have been out there for another hour today and the ball wouldn't have gone in the back of the net. "You have to take it on the chin sometimes. It was an incredible week, but the focus for sure now is on the games ahead," said Kane, who revealed there would be a special presentation of the Ballon d'Or award with the England team during November's international break. After 73 goals for club and country last campaign, Kane has had a slow start by his standards. With eight Bundesliga games played, he has four goals but has turned provider, laying on six assists. Kane set up a late goal for Dayot Upamecano which made it 2-1, but former Wolverhampton forward Fabio Silva scored in the 89th-minute to make it 2-2. Bayern travel to Atletico Madrid on Tuesday but look set to be short staffed, particularly up front. "When you concede late, it always feels a lot worse," Kane said. "But, it's nothing to cry about, we have many games coming up and we've got to put this one behind us and look forward to Tuesday night." The Bavarian giants lost Michael Olise, Ismael Saibari and Serge Gnabry during Saturday's match, adding to an injury list which already includes Jamal Musiala and Luis Diaz. Bayern coach Vincent Kompany is recovering from meningeal irritation. After collapsing on the training pitch last Friday, Kompany was released from hospital on Wednesday but will need more time to recover before returning to the dugout. dwi/lp

item.title: Fabio Silva praises Dortmund's mentality but left annoyed by substitute role
item.description: Fabio Silva praises Dortmund's mentality but left annoyed by substitute role MÜNCHEN ( Bulinews ) Speaking to Bulinews.com after their 2-2 stalemate with FC Bayern , Fabio Silva was proud of Borussia Dortmund's sharp turnaround in mentality. "I'm happy. I think the most important thing was our mentality. After the last game [3-2 DFB-Pokal win] against Bremen, we were not so happy about our performance then. "The coach said it was not our best game and we agreed. We tried to change the mentality and show we are here to fight for titles and we are not afraid of any team," he said. Netting in the 89th-minute to salvage a point for the Westphalians, the Portuguese striker said being a substitute frustrates him but working for the team matters most. "It feels important to help the team. Football is not only about goals. I was there to help the team and try create chances for teammates. I also combine with Serhou [Guirassy] well. "Of course I want to be on the pitch from the start. If I say I'm happy to start on the bench, then I would not be 100 percent honest with you. At first I am of course angry. "But I try to always be positive because I know I am important for the team. If I start on the pitch or bench, I focus on that because we have an amazing squad to fight for titles," he concluded.

item.description: Tottenham Hotspur are finally showing signs of consistency under head coach Roberto de Zerbi [Reuters] The long wait is over. After almost 21 months, Tottenham Hotspur have won three Premier League games in succession again. Spurs cruised to victory on Saturday against Crystal Palace, who were reduced to 10 men after 13 minutes when striker Jean-Philippe Mateta was sent off for an ill-judged lunge at Micky van de Ven. It means Tottenham have moved into the dizzy heights of the top half of the table. Archie Gray and Jan Paul van Hecke scored as Spurs built on a platform established by their first league win of the season at home to Coventry City, then fortified by the outstanding victory at Chelsea - only Spurs' second league triumph at Stamford Bridge in 36 years. But the prevailing mood inside the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium before kick-off against Palace, undoubtedly shaped by the past, was that the visit of a struggling side represented a banana skin rather than an opportunity. Tottenham's players weren't having that, though. Not a bit of it. Instead, Spurs grasped gratefully at the helping hand offered by Mateta's recklessness to end up convincing winners. Three straight wins represent riches indeed. The last time this happened for Tottenham was in February 2025, more than 600 days ago. Three wins is as many as Spurs had in their previous 26 league games combined, in which they drew 10 and lost 13, going back to midway through last season. And, if a further indicator was needed as to just how poor Spurs have been in recent times, this is the first occasion when they have recorded back-to-back home wins in the league for two years. This latest sequence represents consistency of the sort that has eluded Spurs in recent years, the previous incarnation being the consistency of regular defeats and two successive 17th-place finishes in the Premier League. We are witnessing a significant mood shift at Spurs, reflected inside this magnificent arena since the psychological barrier of the vital first league win was crossed against Coventry. Head coach Roberto de Zerbi told BBC Sport's Match Of The Day: "The passion we showed - we didn't lose the focus, the concentration. We made an incredible reaction when we lost the ball. "We could have scored more goals, but we created many chances. We have to be more nasty, especially in the last third of the match, especially in the finishing. I'm happy because I knew before this would be a tough game." De Zerbi pleaded for patience for his big summer acquisitions, with midfield duo Sandro Tonali, a £100m arrival from Newcastle United, and £85m signing Mateus Fernandes, who came from West Ham United, both starting slowly. While any optimistic verdict on Spurs in recent times always comes with natural caution attached, the expensive pair are now showing signs of why De Zerbi was prepared to pay such prices to make them part of his transformation. item.title: ‘It’s a disaster’: Former Colts quarterback calls out owner for being on sidelines during games
item.description: Credit: Robert Scheer-USA TODAY Sports Carlie Irsay-Gordon took over as principal owner and CEO of the Indianapolis Colts after her father, longtime owner Jim Irsay, passed away in 2025, and she has been a fixture on the sideline. Irsay-Gordon was heavily involved in the franchise even before becoming principal owner, having spent over a decade as vice chair and co-owner, but since ascending to the role of principal owner, she has taken on a very hands-on approach during games and stands on the Colts’ sideline wearing a headset and talking to coaches. One former Colts quarterback, Sean Salisbury, who played for the franchise in 1987, thinks Irsay-Gordon needs to stop. “I told you when the season started when an owner stands on the sideline taking notes, you’re f*cked,” Salisbury said. “I know people are going to focus on men or women, I don’t care what the gender is…. Sean Salisbury Went off of Carlie Irsay-Gordon “I told you when the season started when an owner stands on the sideline taking notes, you’re f*cked. I know people are going to focus on men or women, I don’t care what the gender is …. I don’t care if you’re SpongeBob Squarepants …. Players do not like to feel like they’re being micro-managed.” https://t.co/efyWK1hWTC — uSTADIUM (@uSTADIUM) October 31, 2026 “I don’t care if you’re SpongeBob SquarePants. That is no place for the owner to be [on the sideline]. I have a lot of respect for the Irsays, I do. But the second you come downstairs during a game – not during the end – I’m telling you it’s a disaster. … Players do not like to feel like they’re being micro-managed.” Irsay-Gordon has explained being on the sidelines as her gaining the best possible understanding of how the team functions. “I think one of the things that I learned in going through, even as back as when we hired Chuck Pagano (in 2012), is that sort of accelerated my, ‘I need to learn more about this,’” she said in June of 2025 . “‘I need to be able to say, is this person full of BS? Do they even know what they’re talking about? And I think one of the things that being on the headset has really helped me learn is to the question earlier, it’s such a complex organism of football team and how it operates.” However, Salisbury isn’t alone in thinking her behavior is out of line. The Ringer’s Bill Simmons said that he’d seen enough of it earlier this month. The Colts are 2-5 and in the middle of a fire sale, so the reality is that their owner trying to learn the way her team operates is far from their most pressing concern. item.title: Max Verstappen will have no say in 2027 Racing Bulls driver line-up, says Red Bull boss
item.description: Motorsport photo Red Bull Racing CEO and team principal Laurent Mekies has explained that Racing Bulls alone will decide its Formula 1 driver line-up for 2027 and that Max Verstappen will not have a say despite his clash with Liam Lawson in Mexico. Both Verstappen and Lawson were handed a one-place grid penalty for the Mexican Grand Prix after making contact during the second practice session on Friday. The four-time champion argued it was "not very smart behaviour" from Lawson while speaking to the media after the session. "Well, I don't think it's called unlucky. Maybe not very smart behaviour, what he was trying to do there," the Dutchman explained. "I mean, at the end of the day it's not going to change my weekend, but if I were him I would act a little bit smarter. Also, when you're fighting for your seat, it's not very smart behaviour." Lawson's contract with the Red Bull sister team expires at the end of 2026, but Mekies insisted that Verstappen and Red Bull would have no sway over the Racing Bulls driver line-up. Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing "No, I think you know you have to separate both aspects. You have some things that were very unnecessary on the track and therefore are frustrating for the drivers involved and frustrating for the teams involved, and this is probably what you hear with Max's answer, and then there are driver decisions," Mekies told Sky Sports F1. "Racing Bulls [driver line-up is] down to them and only down to them." When asked to clarify if Verstappen could influence Racing Bulls' driver decisions, Mekies added: "Max knows motorsport far too much to be influenced by a single episode anyway. I think so far we've been on the back foot. "The other three top teams have been somehow extracting a bit more than us, but the weekend is not finished. The guys have been putting the best shot at the last modification we can do to the car. "Let's see if we can get a bit closer to the top. When things were very bad this morning, we were about three and a half tenths away. If we can close a bit of that gap, it should put us back in the mix." item.title: "We have to get out of this together" – Karius sums up Schalke's struggles after another defeat
item.description: "We have to get out of this together" – Karius sums up Schalke's struggles after another defeat FC Schalke 04 are winless in their last six games, having followed a 2-0 DFB-Pokal exit against Dynamo Dresden with a 0-2 Bundesliga defeat to RB Leipzig at the Veltins-Arena on Saturday. After the game, Schalke goalkeeper Loris Karius didn't mince his words when assessing the club's struggles. “We have to get out of this together. It's a shit situation,” Karius admitted in an interview with Sky. “It's not getting any easier. We have to work, work, work. Score goals, score goals, score goals.” Schalke coach Miron Muslic, meanwhile, came to his team's defence. “We really tried everything within our capabilities. I have no criticism of the team. We threw ourselves into every challenge,” the coach insisted. Despite suffering another defeat, Muslic even felt that his side had shown signs of improvement. “We took a step forward today, even if it was a very, very small one,” he noted. “We have to keep going and learn quickly.” The result leaves Schalke in 16th place, but they could be overtaken by 1. FC Union Berlin on Sunday if the capital club manage to pick up at least a point against 1. FC Köln. The Royal Blues are also in danger of setting an unwanted record: only FC St. Pauli have previously gone without scoring in their first five home matches of a Bundesliga season.

item.title: Bergen Catholic pulls away late to defeat DePaul in 'Campanile Bowl'
item.description: ORADELL – Bergen Catholic versus DePaul, aka the Campanile Bowl, was again won by the football team coached by the older brother. Coach Vito Campanile and Bergen Catholic pulled away in the second half and secured the 28-14 victory in the final minute over brother Nick and DePaul in their regular-season finales on Oct. 31. “This is the game that’s never easy for me,” said Vito Campanile, who is 3-0 in a family series that began in 2022. “It’s the only time you ever win and you feel somewhat of a little bit of a dent in you, if that makes sense.” “It’s always really tough, but it’s not about that,” Nick Campanile said. “Obviously, Vito’s taught me more than anybody on the planet, I love him to death and obviously respect him more than anybody. I wouldn’t be where I am right now without him, but it’s about the kids, and you try to block that part out as best as you can.” Junior quarterback Trey Tagliaferri threw for 171 yards and a TD and ran for a score to lead Bergen Catholic (5-4). Junior running back Anthony Cristiano and versatile senior Bryan Porter also ran for TDs for the Crusaders. DePaul tied the score, 7-7, with 12 seconds left in the second quarter on senior running back Sean Nevers’ 1-yard run. The Spartans tied it in the third, 14-14, on junior quarterback Frank Morano’s 21-yard score to junior Gavin Sblendorio. Bergen Catholic secured the win in the final minutes. Tagliaferri threw a 1-yard TD pass to sophomore Cruz Araujo for a 28-14 lead with 1:22 remaining. Crusaders senior defensive back Amar’e Newell sealed the win with an interception with just under a minute remaining “It’s a family affair,” said Bergen Catholic junior TE/DE Rocky Rosenberg, on the field for more than 100 plays,” but we treat it like every other game. The preparation is the same, and you just stay ready.” Players of the game Bryan Porter, Bergen Catholic: Porter carried 17 times for 93 yards and a TD, with most of his runs to the outside. He also caught six passes for 48 yards. Trey Tagliaferri, Bergen Catholic: Tagliaferri was 21 for 25 for 171 yards, one TD and no interceptions. He scored the first TD midway through the second quarter on a 5-yard run. They said it “A grind-it-out, playoff-type win, a tough, tough football game,” Vito Campanile said. “They have some great stuff schematically and gave us some fits. It was just a back-and-forth battle and we got that service break late and made the most of it.” “Obviously disappointed,” Nick Campanile said. “We had our chances in that game. I felt we left a lot of points on the field in the first half, and then it came back to bite us.” My take It’s playoff time now, with Bergen Catholic heading into Non-Public A and DePaul seeking a third consecutive title in Non-Public B. Seedings will be released Nov. 1. Bergen Catholic, ranked No. 8 in the USA TODAY NETWORK New Jersey Super 25 , needs to run the ball better and produce more big plays. item.title: The Packers can’t run block
item.description: (Photo by Amy Lemus/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images Stating the complete obvious, but the Green Bay Packers’ running game has reached a level of hopelessness that seems almost statistically impossible. Coming into Thursday night, the Carolina Panthers ranked a paltry 30th in EPA allowed per rush. If there was ever going to be any sort of “get right” game for the offensive line, it was going to happen against Carolina. They had just been pummeled by Tampa Bay four days earlier, facing 48 carries and allowing a 94th percentile rushing success rate to the Buccaneers. They were tired, they were on the road, and they are a bad run defense. And it didn’t matter. Despite starting left guard Aaron Banks returning to the lineup last night, he struggled more than anyone else. In watching all of the Packers’ 25 running back carries, I credited Banks with seven errors or lost blocks that lead to the play not working as intended (either leading to the tackle or disrupting the intended play design). That’s a rate of 28%. His fellow guard Laken Tomlinson, playing on the right side now after Banks’ return, was credited with four errors. Emergency third-string center John Williams was credited with three, including a really bad whiff near the goal line. Josh Jacobs somehow scored on this but good grief John Williams whiffed hard pic.twitter.com/K57xfSxaqF — rcon14 (@rcon14) October 30, 2026 The tackles were better, with Belton credited for two, and Morgan’s only error involving missing the linebacker on the Jacobs toss to the left. item.title: No Elandon Roberts for Steelers Battle vs. Browns
item.description: Pittsburgh Steelers linebacker Elandon Roberts in a game against the Los Angeles Chargers on Sept. 22, 2024. -- Ed Thompson / Steelers Now The Pittsburgh Steelers faithful will have to wait at least one more week for the return of popular inside linebacker Elandon Roberts. Roberts was not elevated from the Steelers’ practice squad by the Steelers before Saturday’s deadline, meaning he will not be eligible to play in Week 8, when the Steelers host the Cleveland Browns. The Steelers called up two others from the practice squad, signing wide receiver Brandon Smith and elevating wide receiver Brandon Johnson with a slew of injuries at wide receiver. Wide receivers Michael Pittman Jr., Roman Wilson remain on injured reserve, while Ben Skowronek is questionable to play as he attempts to return from a calf injury. Roberts r e-joined the Steelers via the practice squad on Oct. 12. The 32-year-old had been one of the team’s final cuts coming out of training camp. Pittsburgh Steelers inside linebacker Elandon Roberts during a game against the New York Jets on Oct. 21, 2024. — Ed Thompson / Steelers Now Roberts was with the Steelers from 2023-24, and then spent last season with the Las Vegas Raiders, where he played for current Steelers defensive coordinator Patrick Graham . He rejoined the team this summer, late in training camp, “I enjoyed him in training camp,” head coach Mike McCarthy said on Monday. “I thought he did a nice job. I think timing was a little bit to do with his opportunity. Once again, we’re trying to get better. All these opportunities that we are creating for players. The changes that you make, we’re trying to improve the team. He’s a veteran. He’s done great things throughout his career, but this man just wants to win. Can’t have enough people like that.” The Steelers do not have any injuries or obvious need for an additional linebacker to dress. Hank Brown threw two first-half touchdown passes, and Iowa’s defense smothered No. 25 Wisconsin in a 30-0 shutout to retain the Heartland Trophy on Saturday afternoon. The Hawkeyes (6-2, 3-2 Big Ten) earned their fifth straight win over Wisconsin, outscoring the Badgers 109-10 in their last three meetings. The shutout also leveled the historic 100-game rivalry —dating back to 1894—at 49-49-2 . Brown, who had split snaps with Jeremy Hecklinski, was surgical early, completing 16 of 18 passes for 190 yards in the first half alone before finishing 20-of-24 for 222 yards. Xavier Williams stepped into the primary ball-carrier role after Kamari Moulton's season-ending injury, grinding out 78 yards on 20 carries as Iowa out-gained Wisconsin 362-235. MORE: Which unbeaten FBS team will lose first? Sizing up Miami, Utah and UCLA chances to finish 12-0 Iowa's defense held Wisconsin (5-3, 3-2) to just 52 rushing yards on 2.2 yards per carry and forced Badgers starting quarterback Colton Joseph out of rhythm. Joseph completed 5 of 14 passes for 90 yards before being replaced by freshman Ryan Hopkins, who finished 8-of-13 for 93 yards and an interception. The Hawkeyes set the tone on their opening possession, taking a 3-0 lead when Brown connected with DJ Vonnahme on a 45-yard strike up the left sideline, setting up Caden Buhr’s 24-yard field goal. MORE: 5 things to watch in Week 9: Judgment Day comes for Lincoln Riley, Buckeyes QBs After forcing a three-and-out, Iowa marched 75 yards in 12 plays. Brown extended the drive with a 15-yard scramble on third down, hit Tony Diaz on a 17-yard crossing pattern, and capped the possession with a 4-yard touchdown pass to Vonnahme. Wisconsin mounted its lone sustained threat late in the second quarter, marching 86 yards to the Iowa 1-yard line. The Hawkeyes’ defense held firm on fourth-and-goal, stopping Abu Sama III for a 1-yard loss with 4:22 left in the half to maintain a 20-0 cushion at the break. Vonnahme added a 2-yard touchdown run midway through the third quarter to push the margin to 27-0. Buhr drilled his third field goal of the afternoon—a 54-yard strike—late in the third quarter to cap the scoring at 30-0.
